I have only 4.1 mu, so I will keep the plan simple and put most of my land into the crop that fits my current system best, which is stevia, while still keeping some cotton because I already know how to grow it and it spreads my risk. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I do not want a plan that depends on too much labor at one time, so I will use improved seed, do rotary tillage to save effort, and rely on my well for timely irrigation. For stevia, I will push a bit more fertilizer and water because I want steady leaf production and good quality. For cotton, I will manage inputs more carefully and not overdo them on such a small farm. I will still use pesticides when needed because I cannot afford major pest losses on 4.1 mu. My main goal this year is stable output and lower risk, not chasing the very highest yield.
